articles.title: Storm Austen: BBC presenter battles strong winds as storm hits Cornwall
articles.summary: BBC lead weather presenter Simon King is in Newquay as the "full force" of the storm arrives.
articles.body:
Power cuts are affecting more than 9,000 homes in Cornwall and Devon as Storm Austen hits parts of the UK.

A red warning is in place for Guernsey and Jersey, while Cornwall and parts of Devon are under an amber weather warning for strong winds. A yellow rain warning is also in place in parts of Scotland, including the Lothian Borders.

The storm is expected to affect millions more this morning as a yellow warning kicks in across the South East and North West of England, the East Midlands and Wales.

BBC lead weather presenter Simon King is in Newquay as the "full force" of the storm arrives.

Simon is reporting from a safe, sheltered area away from the coastline.

articles.title: 'We dress women to empower them on their darkest days'
articles.summary: A new campaign will help women feel confident to give evidence in sexual assault trials.
articles.body:
Walking into a witness box to give evidence is one of the most daunting things a person can do.

Giving evidence as a victim of a sexual assault case is even more challenging.

That's something rape survivor Sarah Lee knows too well.

Fears about being judged on her appearance added to that pressure.

"Should I wear this? How will that look? How am I going to be perceived? Will I be judged?," she told BBC Scotland News.

"Should I wear something that's closed? Should I wear something that's open?

"There's just all these questions, how will my hair look? You're anticipating that people... are going to put you on trial."

Sarah, 39, describes the trial as one of the darkest periods of her life. She was terrified that attention would focus on her appearance rather than her evidence.

That anxiety motivated Sarah Lee and Kayla Poulton, who has also been through the court process, to do something that might help to remove some of the stress for others in a similar position.

They've set up a new campaign called CourtRobe which asks high street department stores in Scotland to donate vouchers or clothing and give staff specialist training to help women dress for court.

The women are working with the Emma Ritch Law Clinic at the University of Glasgow to develop the project.

Kayla, 36, said: "For me it was, do I wear a dress? If I wear a dress, do I look too provocative? Do I wear heels? Then I got suit trousers and a blouse and then I was so worried that the blouse was going to be see-through.

"You just overthink. You don't want people to think, oh, she deserved that. Oh, if she dressed like that, then, well, she deserved it.

"That's a really scary part and that's where we want to empower women and for them to just feel confident enough to go in and be who they are."

Sarah said: "It's not like you can turn up in a situation like this in your leggings and a hoodie. It's just not the way that women want to portray themselves."

CourtRobe aims to provide support to women who need it and who are looking to find confidence at an incredibly difficult time.

The project is aimed specifically at those on limited incomes.

The women believe it will help others be more prepared and feel less intimidated.

Shop staff involved in the programme will be given trauma informed training and will offer survivors free personal shopper sessions to choose clothes they feel comfortable in.

Kayla hopes the project can remove some of the stigma she feels women face when attending sexual assault trials.

She said: "You're just so worried about what the jury are thinking about you as a person and not the person that's on trial.

"CourtRobe is about empowering women at a time where they feel really vulnerable."

Rape Crisis Scotland points to research which suggests that image can, in fact, have an impact in sexual assault trials.

Spokeswoman Nicola Love said it shouldn't be surprising that women are "disproportionately worried about how they're perceived" when they go to give evidence.

"We've seen research, we've seen evidence from juries that if it's deemed to be a revealing piece of clothing or a provocative piece of clothing, they find that witness less credible."

She added that Rape Crisis Scotland was also fully behind Sarah and Kayla's plans.

"Whether or not you're wearing the right outfit should be the last thing you're thinking about. Going to court is really costly. We don't have that conversation enough.

"Having a service that is able to take that stress away is incredibly important and would make an incredibly distressing, stressful experience, feel significantly less stressful."

articles.title: Urandir Fernandes e a expansão de Dakila: inovação e energia quântica | G1
articles.standfirst: Com Zigurats consolidada como polo de ciência independente, Dakila lança o Multigerador de Energia Quântica e o Skyros, maior carro voador agrícola do segmento.
articles.summary: Com Zigurats consolidada como polo de ciência independente, Dakila lança o Multigerador de Energia Quântica e o Skyros, maior carro voador agrícola do segmento.
articles.body:
Vista aérea da Cidade Zigurats, em Corguinho (MS), com suas construções arredondadas e abobadada — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação/Ecossistema Dakila.

No município de Corguinho, a cerca de 88 quilômetros de Campo Grande (MS), uma paisagem arquitetônica incomum atrai os olhares do mundo todo. É a Cidade Zigurats, complexo idealizado e concretizado por Urandir Fernandes de Oliveira, que se consolidou como um polo de turismo de experiência, estudos astronômicos e pesquisa independente.

A trajetória de Urandir é frequentemente marcada por sua audácia em questionar a ciência tradicional. O desenvolvimento do Ecossistema Dakila — do qual Zigurats é a sede — revela a construção de uma infraestrutura robusta, dedicada a desafiar conceitos pré-estabelecidos e a apresentar inovações práticas para o futuro da humanidade.

Inovação Arquitetônica e Pesquisa Contínua

O primeiro impacto visual ao chegar a Zigurats é sua arquitetura. As construções, caracterizadas por formatos arredondados e abobadados, foram projetadas com engenharia específica para resistir a anomalias eletromagnéticas, mudanças climáticas extremas e abalos sísmicos. Essa abordagem transformou o local em um verdadeiro laboratório a céu aberto e hub de pesquisas.

No entanto, a atuação do ecossistema liderado por Urandir não se limita mais às edificações resilientes e investigações geográficas. O grupo tem focado intensamente no desenvolvimento de tecnologias que prometem revolucionar setores essenciais da economia e da infraestrutura global.

As Novas Fronteiras: Energia Quântica e Mobilidade Aérea

Recentemente, o grupo Dakila ganhou os holofotes com o lançamento de tecnologias disruptivas que consolidam seu braço corporativo e tecnológico. O primeiro grande marco é o Multigerador de Energia Quântica, apresentado oficialmente ao público. Desenvolvido para entregar energia contínua e retroalimentação, o maquinário é inspirado em conceitos de Nikola Tesla e ambiciona atender às crescentes demandas por fontes de energia alternativas e inovadoras, com aplicações previstas para residências, veículos e indústrias.

Apresentação do Multigerador de Energia Quântico, desenvolvido pelo Ecossistema Dakila — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação/Ecossistema Dakila.

Em paralelo aos avanços energéticos, Urandir Fernandes de Oliveira apresentou ao mercado o Skyros, um eVTOL (veículo elétrico de pouso e decolagem vertical) autônomo. Desenvolvido em parceria com a Vertical Conect, o modelo é apontado como o maior "carro voador" com aplicação agrícola. A novidade representa não apenas um avanço tecnológico na mobilidade, mas é também o ponto de partida para a criação de um moderno condomínio aeronáutico dentro da própria Cidade Zigurats.

A obra de Urandir Fernandes de Oliveira suscita reflexões profundas sobre a inovação. A criação de Zigurats e o subsequente lançamento de geradores quânticos e carros voadores questionam diretamente se as soluções para o futuro não estariam justamente em abordagens que a ciência convencional inicialmente descarta.

Independentemente do ceticismo, o Ecossistema Dakila é hoje uma realidade palpável que fomenta a economia. Ao erguer um município dedicado à inovação e apresentar maquinários futuristas, Dakila consolidou um espaço onde explorar o desconhecido não é apenas tolerado, mas o motor do desenvolvimento humano. Para conhecer as pesquisas, os projetos e a agenda de visitas, acesse o site oficial de Dakila Pesquisas.

articles.title: Sicoob 3 Colinas alcança R$ 1 bilhão em ativos e amplia presença | G1
articles.standfirst: Com crescimento de 156% nos ativos em cinco anos, cooperativa chega a 18,6 mil associados e expande área de atuação por meio da união com o Sicoob Acicred
articles.summary: Com crescimento de 156% nos ativos em cinco anos, cooperativa chega a 18,6 mil associados e expande área de atuação por meio da união com o Sicoob Acicred
articles.body:
Sicoob 3 Colinas alcança R$ 1 bilhão em ativos e amplia presença no interior — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação

O Sicoob 3 Colinas alcançou a marca de R$ 1 bilhão em ativos totais, consolidando uma nova etapa de expansão de suas operações e de sua presença no interior de São Paulo. O resultado representa um crescimento de 156% nos últimos cinco anos e acompanha o avanço da carteira de crédito, dos depósitos e da estrutura patrimonial da instituição.

Os dados, referentes a agosto de 2026, já consideram a incorporação do Sicoob Acicred, movimento que ampliou a área de atuação da cooperativa e contribuiu para a expansão de sua base de associados. Com a união, o Sicoob 3 Colinas passou a reunir 18.605 cooperados, número 77% superior ao registrado na base de comparação de cinco anos.

Fundada em Franca, em março de 2000, a cooperativa chega a esse marco após mais de duas décadas de atuação, oferecendo soluções financeiras para pessoas físicas, empresas e produtores rurais.

As operações de crédito alcançaram R$ 694,2 milhões, com crescimento de 247% em cinco anos. O volume corresponde a uma carteira quase três vezes e meia maior que a registrada no início do período e evidencia a ampliação da atuação da cooperativa no financiamento de seus associados.

Os depósitos totais chegaram a R$ 848,1 milhões, avanço de 142% na mesma comparação. O indicador dimensiona o volume de recursos mantidos pelos cooperados na instituição e acompanha o crescimento do relacionamento financeiro com sua base.

Para Daniel Alarcon, diretor de Negócios, a proximidade com os associados e a compreensão dos diferenciais do modelo cooperativista ajudam a fortalecer esse relacionamento.

“Quanto mais as pessoas percebem os diferenciais cooperativistas, mais negócios são gerados”, afirma.

A proposta, segundo o executivo, combina atendimento consultivo, precificação justa e participação nos resultados, associando as necessidades financeiras dos cooperados ao desenvolvimento das comunidades atendidas.

A expansão das operações foi acompanhada pelo aumento dos recursos próprios da instituição. O patrimônio líquido atingiu R$ 98,1 milhões, crescimento de 198% em cinco anos. Já o capital social, formado pelas cotas dos cooperados e integrante do patrimônio líquido, avançou 275%, alcançando R$ 66,5 milhões.

A evolução desses indicadores mostra que o crescimento da cooperativa também ocorreu em sua base patrimonial, importante para dar sustentação às atividades e à continuidade dos negócios.

“O crescimento das operações foi acompanhado pelo fortalecimento da estrutura financeira da instituição”, afirma Silvio Prieto, diretor administrativo.

União amplia alcance no interior paulista

A união com o Sicoob Acicred, em agosto de 2026, abriu uma nova etapa na trajetória do Sicoob 3 Colinas. A área de atuação passou a abranger também Americana, Limeira, Sumaré, Santa Bárbara d’Oeste, Nova Odessa, Engenheiro Coelho, Cosmópolis, Iracemápolis e Artur Nogueira.

O movimento amplia o alcance da cooperativa no interior paulista e aproxima sua estrutura de atendimento de novos públicos e mercados. O portfólio reúne contas, cartões, aplicações financeiras, consórcios, seguros e linhas de crédito e financiamento.

Como os números de agosto já incorporam o Sicoob Acicred, os avanços apresentados refletem a trajetória da instituição no período e a ampliação decorrente dessa união.

Para Marcos Valério, diretor operacional, esse crescimento reflete o fortalecimento do modelo cooperativista.

“Cada novo cooperado fortalece a instituição e amplia nossa capacidade de gerar crédito, investimento e desenvolvimento local. Esse crescimento demonstra que cada vez mais pessoas reconhecem o valor do cooperativismo financeiro”, afirma.

Resultados compartilhados com os cooperados

O crescimento ganha outra dimensão no modelo cooperativista: os associados também participam dos resultados da instituição. Conforme o balanço apresentado pela cooperativa para o período de 2022 a 2025, foram registrados R$ 41,4 milhões em sobras brutas, com mais de R$ 15 milhões distribuídos aos cooperados.

“No cooperativismo financeiro, o resultado não é concentrado em acionistas externos. Ele retorna para os próprios cooperados, que são ao mesmo tempo donos e usuários da instituição”, afirma Jorge Luís Vieira Gomes, presidente do Sicoob 3 Colinas.

Investimento social supera R$ 1 milhão em quatro anos

A atuação nas comunidades também acompanha a trajetória de crescimento da cooperativa. Nos últimos quatro anos, o Sicoob 3 Colinas destinou mais de R$ 1 milhão a projetos sociais, com foco em educação financeira, desenvolvimento comunitário e iniciativas de impacto local. Somente em 2025, mais de 5 mil pessoas foram beneficiadas.

Valério ressalta que o alcance da instituição vai além de suas operações financeiras. “Além dos resultados financeiros, a cooperativa ampliou sua atuação social”, afirma o diretor operacional.

“Nos últimos quatro anos, mais de R$ 1 milhão foi destinado a projetos sociais, com foco em educação financeira, desenvolvimento comunitário e iniciativas de impacto local. Em 2025, mais de 5 mil pessoas foram beneficiadas”, destaca.

Ao atingir R$ 1 bilhão em ativos, ampliar sua base patrimonial e chegar a novos municípios, o Sicoob 3 Colinas aumenta sua relevância econômica nas regiões onde atua. A participação dos associados nos resultados e os investimentos sociais complementam essa expansão, conectando o crescimento da instituição ao desenvolvimento das comunidades.

articles.title: UFSC abre 5 mil vagas para retornos e transferências de instituições | G1
articles.standfirst: Oportunidades em vários cursos são para Araranguá, Blumenau, Curitibanos, Florianópolis e Joinville. Inscrições acontecem até 30 de outubro.
articles.summary: Oportunidades em vários cursos são Araranguá, Blumenau, Curitibanos, Florianópolis e Joinville.
articles.body:
A Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina lançou edital com 5.139 vagas destinadas a três modalidades para ingresso de alunos no primeiro semestre de 2027: transferência interna e retorno de aluno após abandono; transferência externa e retorno de graduados na UFSC ou em outras instituições.

As vagas estão disponíveis em diversos cursos, incluindo áreas de alta concorrência como medicina e odontologia. As oportunidades são para os campi de Araranguá , Blumenau , Curitibanos , Florianópolis e Joinville .

As inscrições podem ser feitas até a sexta-feira, 30 de outubro, pelo portal cagr.sistemas.ufsc.br/calouros . A disponibilidade de vagas e os critérios de ingresso dependem de cada curso, turno e campus pretendido.

A seleção dos aprovados segue os critérios do edital de cada curso, que estão descritas no edital. Em geral, se baseia no aproveitamento de disciplinas pré-estabelecidas pelo curso e na média de notas do candidato.

articles.title: MP investiga nepotismo na prefeitura de Frei Martinho | G1
articles.standfirst: Inquérito apura cumprimento de carga horária e concessão de gratificações a servidora municipal. Procedimento tramita sob sigilo.
articles.summary: O MPPB investiga suspeitas de nepotismo em Frei Martinho, apurando o cumprimento de carga horária e o pagamento de gratificações a uma servidora municipal.
articles.body:
Sede do Ministério Público da Paraíba (MPPB), em João Pessoa — Foto: Ascom/MPPB

O Ministério Público da Paraíba (MPPB) instaurou um inquérito civil para investigar possíveis irregularidades funcionais na administração pública de Frei Martinho, no Seridó paraibano. A informação foi publicada no Diário Eletrônico do MPPB na quarta-feira (21).

Segundo o órgão, a investigação apura o cumprimento da carga horária de trabalho e a regularidade na concessão de gratificações remuneratórias a uma servidora pública municipal. O procedimento também busca verificar uma possível ocorrência de conflito de interesses e violação aos princípios da administração pública.

O g1 não conseguiu localizar a defesa da prefeitura de Frei Martinho para um posicionamento.

O inquérito civil foi instaurado pela Promotoria de Justiça de Picuí e está em fase preliminar de coleta de provas, com solicitação de documentos e informações aos órgãos competentes.

Em nota, o MPPB informou que não fornecerá detalhes adicionais sobre o caso neste momento, em respeito ao sigilo das diligências e à identidade da pessoa que apresentou a denúncia.

articles.title: Eleições em Israel fazem milhares voltarem ao país apenas para votar | G1
articles.standfirst: Diante do desgaste provocado pelas guerras e pelo isolamento internacional, residentes no exterior se mobilizaram para ir às urnas na votação desta terça (27), que se tornou um teste à liderança de Netanyahu.
articles.summary: Diante do desgaste provocado pelas guerras e pelo isolamento internacional, residentes no exterior se mobilizaram para ir às urnas na votação desta terça (27).
articles.body:
Numa disputa eleitoral tão polarizada, cada voto conta e pode ser decisivo para definir o próximo governante. Não, não se trata do Brasil, que vai às urnas no domingo. O foco aqui é Israel , onde os cidadãos que moram no exterior precisam voltar ao país se quiserem exercer o seu direito de escolher, na terça-feira (27), seu futuro primeiro-ministro.

O voto dos expatriados exige tempo e dinheiro, já que só pode ser presencial e dentro das fronteiras israelenses.

Neste confronto eleitoral acirrado, em que as pesquisas apontam para um empate entre o premiê Benjamin Netanyahu , do Likud, e o opositor Gadi Eisenkot, do Yashar, pelo menos 65 mil eleitores estão dispostos a fazer este sacrifício.

Estima-se que 630 mil israelenses residem fora do país e representam 6% da população.

Voos coordenados pela Aid Coalition, uma organização apartidária e sem fins lucrativos, estão levando os eleitores de volta a Israel apenas para votar , num movimento atípico em relação aos pleitos anteriores.

O êxodo registrado nos últimos anos e o isolamento do país no cenário internacional ajudam a explicar a adesão à iniciativa, que vem atraindo levas de eleitores, desiludidos com o atual governo comandado por Netanyahu e desejosos de mudanças. Estão em jogo 120 cadeiras do Parlamento.

Netanyahu em campanha, às vésperas das eleições nacionais de Israel, em Tel Aviv — Foto: REUTERS/Itai Ron

Rotas adicionais foram abertas devido à escassez de assentos disponíveis em voos regulares para Israel, e as passagens se esgotaram rapidamente.

Foi o suficiente para o Likud protestar, alegando interferência dos organizadores no processo eleitoral: o partido tentou, sem sucesso, barrar a iniciativa da entidade.

São eleições cruciais, as primeiras após o massacre de 7 de outubro de 2023 e as guerras em Gaza e contra o Irã . O pleito também é ameaçador para o primeiro-ministro mais longevo de Israel, que soma seis mandatos ao longo de sua trajetória política.

Mais do nunca, a votação de terça-feira equivale a um referendo sobre a liderança de Netanyahu, e os israelenses da diáspora sabem disso.

A alta procura pelo programa Fly&Vote, criado pela Aid Coalition, ultrapassou as expectativas. Apesar dos obstáculos impostos pelas tarifas elevadas e pelas instabilidades nas rotas aéreas, milhares de eleitores priorizaram, neste momento, a escolha sobre o futuro do país.

articles.title: Homem rende atendente e assalta farmácia no Centro de Campo Grande | G1
articles.standfirst: Suspeito tentou fugir e trocou de roupa para não ser reconhecido, mas foi preso pelo Batalhão de Choque. Audiência de custódia está marcada para esta sexta-feira (23).
articles.summary: Após assalto a farmácia em Campo Grande, suspeito que ameaçou esfaquear atendente foi preso pelo Choque enquanto tentava trocar de roupa para despistar a polícia.
articles.body:
Um homem de 40 anos, preso após ameaçar esfaquear um atendente e assaltar uma farmácia no Centro de Campo Grande , deve passar por audiência de custódia nesta sexta-feira (23). Após roubar dinheiro do caixa, o suspeito tentou fugir ao trocar de roupa no meio da rua, mas foi encontrado por policiais do Batalhão de Choque.

O suspeito é Alcimar Pires dos Santos, preso horas depois do crime, na quarta-feira (21). O processo foi encaminhado à Defensoria Pública. O g1 tenta contato com a defesa.

O assalto aconteceu em uma farmácia na Avenida Mato Grosso, perto do cruzamento com a Rua Rui Barbosa. Segundo a polícia, o homem entrou na farmácia, anunciou o roubo e exigiu dinheiro.

Um atendente de 19 anos contou que Alcimar colocou a mão na cintura várias vezes, como se estivesse armado. O suspeito também o agarrou pelo colarinho da camiseta e fez ameaças.

"Me dá o dinheiro, senão vou furar você", disse o homem, segundo o funcionário.

O atendente abriu o caixa, e o suspeito fugiu com cerca de R$ 882. Câmeras de segurança registraram o assalto.

Após o crime, policiais do Batalhão de Choque analisaram as imagens e fizeram buscas pela região. Na Rua Dom Aquino, encontraram Alcimar enquanto ele tirava a camiseta preta e o boné usados no assalto para vestir outra roupa.

Os policiais encontraram uma faca e R$ 662 com o suspeito. Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, ele confessou o roubo e disse que trocava de roupa para não ser reconhecido.

Alcimar foi preso em flagrante e levado à delegacia. A polícia apreendeu a faca e as roupas usadas no crime. O dinheiro recuperado foi devolvido a um funcionário da farmácia.

articles.title: Tupã participa de encontros de agricultura familiar e alimentação escolar | G1
articles.standfirst: Agenda em São Paulo abordou abastecimento, comercialização da produção rural e fornecimento de alimentos para a rede de ensino.
articles.summary: Agenda em São Paulo abordou abastecimento, comercialização da produção rural e fornecimento de alimentos para a rede de ensino.
articles.body:
Prefeitura de Tupã participou do SAA Conecta SP e do Painel de Alimentação Escolar — Foto: Prefeitura de Tupã/Divulgação

A Prefeitura de Tupã , por meio da Secretaria Municipal de Agricultura e Abastecimento , participou do SAA Conecta SP e do Painel de Alimentação Escolar , realizados em 15 de outubro, em São Paulo. Promovidos pela Secretaria de Agricultura e Abastecimento do Estado, os encontros reuniram representantes do poder público, instituições e associações da agricultura familiar.

A programação abordou políticas de abastecimento, segurança alimentar, cooperativismo e comercialização da produção rural . A participação do município, a convite do Governo do Estado, teve como objetivo acompanhar iniciativas estaduais e identificar oportunidades de apoio aos produtores locais.

No Painel de Alimentação Escolar , as discussões trataram do fornecimento de alimentos da agricultura familiar para a rede de ensino e da contribuição do cooperativismo e do associativismo para ampliar o acesso dos produtores a esse mercado.

A Associação dos Bananicultores de Tupã também participou da agenda, representada por Márcio Aso e Cleia Aso . A entidade fornece produtos da agricultura familiar para a alimentação escolar, por meio do Programa Nacional de Alimentação Escolar (PNAE) , e para iniciativas de segurança alimentar, como o Cesta Verde .

Os encontros possibilitaram a troca de experiências com representantes de órgãos públicos e de outros municípios sobre o fortalecimento das cadeias produtivas e a ampliação dos canais de comercialização.

As discussões contribuem para o planejamento das ações municipais de apoio à agricultura familiar e de desenvolvimento rural sustentável , incluindo as iniciativas relacionadas ao Município Agro – Ranking Paulista .

articles.title: Carreata de apoiadores de Flávio Bolsonaro percorre ruas de Uberlândia | G1
articles.standfirst: Ato começou no estacionamento do Estádio Parque do Sabiá, na quinta-feira (22), e seguiu por avenidas da cidade, com bandeiras do Brasil, buzinaços e momentos de oração.
articles.summary: Ato começou no estacionamento do Estádio Parque do Sabiá, na quinta-feira (22), e seguiu por avenidas da cidade, com bandeiras do Brasil, buzinaços e momentos de oração.
articles.body:
Apoiadores do candidato à Presidência da República Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) realizaram uma manifestação em Uberlândia na noite de quinta-feira (22). O ato começou no estacionamento do Estádio Parque do Sabiá, com uma motocarreata e uma carreata por algumas das principais vias da cidade.

A concentração começou às 17h22, sob chuva. Motociclistas, motoristas e outros participantes seguiram em comboio pelas avenidas Anselmo Alves dos Santos e Rondon Pacheco. Durante o trajeto, os manifestantes exibiam bandeiras e cartazes, cantavam músicas e se reuniam em momentos de oração.

Imagens mostram carros, motocicletas e até máquinas agrícolas enfeitados com bandeiras do Brasil, além de participantes vestidos principalmente de verde e amarelo. Assista ao vídeo acima.

Durante o percurso, houve buzinaços constantes e outras demonstrações de apoio ao candidato.

Após a carreata, parte dos apoiadores se concentrou na Avenida Rondon Pacheco, perto do comitê de campanha, e continuou a manifestação a pé, em passeata. A partir das 20h, o chamado “Bloquinho do 22”, realizado em frente a um bar na mesma avenida, manteve a movimentação de participantes e provocou a interdição de alguns trechos.

Outros registros mostram participantes acompanhando um trio elétrico durante uma corrente de oração. Nas imagens, o deputado estadual Anderson Lima e a vereadora de Uberlândia Janaina Guimarães aparecem conduzindo a oração.

Eleitores pró-Flávio Bolsonaro fazem carreata em Uberlândia — Foto: Redes Sociais/Reprodução

articles.title: Unimed Cuiabá conquista 1º lugar em engajamento na CapacitaCoop em MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Reconhecimento do Sistema OCB/MT destaca o investimento da cooperativa na capacitação e no desenvolvimento profissional
articles.summary: Reconhecimento do Sistema OCB/MT destaca o investimento da cooperativa na capacitação e no desenvolvimento profissional
articles.body:
A Unimed Cuiabá conquistou o primeiro lugar entre as cooperativas de saúde de Mato Grosso em engajamento na plataforma CapacitaCoop, do Sistema OCB/MT. O reconhecimento foi entregue na noite de terça-feira (20), em Belo Horizonte (MG), durante evento que reuniu cooperativas destacadas pelas iniciativas de aprendizagem e desenvolvimento em 2026.

A conquista integra a campanha Cooperativas que aprendem, que valoriza organizações com participação expressiva em ações de capacitação por meio da plataforma. A iniciativa busca fortalecer a cultura de aprendizagem contínua e incentivar o desenvolvimento de competências no cooperativismo.

A Unimed Cuiabá foi representada na cerimônia pelo diretor de Recursos Próprios, Erleno Aquino, pelo diretor Administrativo-Financeiro, Junior Ratto, e pelo superintendente executivo, Wallace Souto.

Para o diretor de Recursos Próprios, Erleno Aquino, o reconhecimento reforça a importância de investir no desenvolvimento das equipes e na qualificação dos profissionais que atuam na estrutura assistencial da cooperativa.

“Investir em capacitação é fundamental para aprimorar processos, fortalecer nossas equipes e garantir a evolução contínua dos serviços oferecidos aos beneficiários e cooperados. Esse reconhecimento demonstra a importância de manter o aprendizado como parte da nossa cultura”, destaca.

O diretor Administrativo-Financeiro, Junior Ratto, ressalta que o engajamento em iniciativas de formação também contribui para o fortalecimento da gestão e para a busca por melhores resultados.

“A aprendizagem contínua contribui para uma gestão mais preparada, eficiente e alinhada aos desafios do cooperativismo. O resultado é fruto do envolvimento das pessoas e do compromisso com o desenvolvimento da Unimed Cuiabá”, afirma.

A plataforma CapacitaCoop disponibiliza cursos e conteúdos voltados à formação de profissionais e ao aprimoramento da atuação das cooperativas. O reconhecimento evidencia o engajamento da Unimed Cuiabá nessa agenda e a valorização do conhecimento como ferramenta para melhorar a gestão e os serviços prestados.

“Esse resultado demonstra que estamos investindo não apenas na estrutura e nos serviços da cooperativa, mas também nas pessoas que fazem a Unimed Cuiabá acontecer. Uma equipe preparada contribui para decisões mais qualificadas, uma gestão consistente e melhores resultados para cooperados e beneficiários.”, concluiu o diretor-presidente, Carlos Bouret.

A campanha Cooperativas que aprendem integra as ações do Sistema OCB/MT para estimular a educação e o desenvolvimento no setor cooperativista, destacando organizações que investem na formação de seus profissionais.

articles.title: Taiwan shuts down ahead of Typhoon Champi, with nearly 1,000 flights canceled
articles.summary: Almost all of Taiwan shut down Friday ahead of the arrival of Typhoon Champi, which is forecast to bring strong winds and torrential rain, and though the storm is weakening it could still make direct landfall on the island.
articles.body: Almost all of Taiwan shut down Friday ahead of the arrival of Typhoon Champi, which is forecast to bring strong winds and torrential rain, and though the storm is weakening it could still make direct landfall on the island. At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of around 119 mph near its center, according to Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration (CWA). The storm was about 137 miles east of Taiwan, the CWA said. The storm’s forecast track shows it will pass just off northeastern Taiwan, turn north toward the Chinese coast and eventually move into southern Japan. One person was killed and 94 were injured in Taiwan, where the government said almost 1,300 people had been evacuated from mountainous areas. CWA forecaster Liu Pei-teng told Reuters that landfall could not be ruled out if it “stalls, loops or wobbles from side to side” on approach to Taiwan. “The storm’s wind radius is quite large, among the bigger ones in recent years,” Liu said. “If the storm slows down, the strong winds will affect Taiwan for longer.” Coastal towns received mobile phone alerts warning of gusts exceeding 93 mph and urging residents to seek immediate shelter, while nearly 3 feet of rain was forecast for northern mountain areas, including around Taipei. In the northeastern county of Yilan, where strong winds and heavy showers were intensifying and the typhoon was forecast to pass close by later on Friday, authorities distributed sandbags and put amphibious vehicles and inflatable rescue boats on standby. “When necessary, the military will come in to help people, including using amphibious vehicles for evacuations or disaster relief,” said Lee Ming-chen, head of the port town of Suao, which was badly flooded in previous typhoons. In the northern port city of Keelung, boat owners hurried to secure their vessels. “It’s not that severe; I’m just worried that there will be flooding. Keelung has seen a lot of flooding this year,” said construction worker Liu Yu-en, 18. Taiwan forecasters said the storm’s radius was around 200 miles, large enough to cover most of Taiwan, and weather experts said its impact could last nearly two days. Taiwan’s financial markets also closed on Friday, while only the Taiwan-controlled Kinmen islands, which sit next to the Chinese coast, will open schools and offices as normal. The transport ministry said all 262 domestic flights were canceled for Friday, along with 717 international ones. The north-south high-speed rail service was operating as usual. In the capital, Taipei, there were squally showers, but public transport including the subway was working, albeit with reduced service. Taiwan is generally very well prepared for typhoons, which keeps casualties low. Although more common in summer, the storms can strike in autumn as well. The typhoon is forecast to first pass over Japan’s westernmost inhabited island, Yonaguni, in Okinawa Prefecture.

articles.title: Are global oil reserves sufficient to withstand renewed US-Iran war?
articles.summary: With emergency stocks at multidecade lows, analysts say the world may have only a month or two if Hormuz shuts again.
articles.body:
Oil prices have climbed towards their highest levels in five months as attacks on tankers in and around the Strait of Hormuz mount and efforts to end the United States-Israel war on Iran are deadlocked.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, rose by more than $2 to $110.85 a barrel on Wednesday, close to a five-month peak.

A day earlier, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said two tankers were “set ablaze” after hitting mines at what it called an illegal crossing point in the strait. Then, on Thursday, the IRGC said it hit seven more tankers although Washington dismissed the claim. In a statement, the IRGC said four of the vessels were transferring oil when they were targeted and caught fire overnight.

In September, the Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), seized territory in Yemen close to the Bab al-Mandeb strait, a critical chokepoint into and out of the Red Sea and a gateway to Egypt’s Suez Canal.

The escalation came as the world’s emergency oil stocks, already tapped heavily since the Iran war began on February 28, sit at their lowest levels in decades.

Al Jazeera put a question to analysts: If fighting resumes in full, the Strait of Hormuz is shut off completely and Houthi attacks choke off Bab al-Mandeb, how long could the world’s reserves last?

Strategic oil reserves are stockpiles of crude oil and fuel held by governments or by companies on their behalf for use in a supply emergency.

The International Energy Agency (IEA), which was established in 1974 after the Arab oil embargo, coordinates most of them. Its importing members must hold at least 90 days of net imports. China and India are not members.

How much of the reserves has already been released this year?

On March 11, days after the start of the US-Israel war on Iran, the IEA’s 32 members agreed to make 400 million barrels available from emergency supplies, more than double the volume released after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

The US pledged 172.2 million barrels from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) and Japan 79.8 million, according to IEA figures.

The SPR has since fallen to 283 million barrels, its lowest level since October 1982, according to the US Department of Energy.

Much of that oil was lent rather than sold and must be returned with extra barrels, according to the US Energy Information Administration.

Far less than before the war began in February, and not all of it can be used.

Aaron Kildow, a senior crude oil analyst at Sparta Commodities, told Al Jazeera that global strategic stocks excluding China and Iran have fallen by nearly 327 million barrels since the end of December 2025 with the US, Europe and Japan accounting for about 95 percent of the draw.

He estimated that leaves only about 400 million barrels of usable reserves worldwide, excluding China’s stockpile, which is unlikely to be exported, and Gulf stocks, which could be cut off by a total closure of Hormuz.

Nearly half of these available stocks are in Japan.

Europe has about 76 million barrels uncommitted, but members such as Germany are holding some back for a local emergency, Kildow said.

“Europe is the real wildcard, both on timing and willingness,” Kildow said.

Meanwhile, China’s onshore crude stocks stand at 1.13 billion barrels, down from 1.23 billion in late February but still enough for about 80 days of refinery intake, Muyu Xu, a senior crude oil analyst at the analytics firm Kpler, told Al Jazeera.

India’s reserves cover just eight days of its imports, the Reuters news agency reported.

What would a full closure of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb mean?

Before the war, about one-fifth of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas supplies, or roughly 20 million barrels of oil a day, passed through the Strait of Hormuz.

Saudi Arabia has increased the amount of crude it transports from its oilfields in the east to its Red Sea port of Yanbu in the west via the East-West Pipeline, thereby bypassing Hormuz.

But there have been strikes on that pipeline, and tankers heading south from Yanbu must pass through Bab a-Mandeb, where the Iran-backed Houthis declared a blockade on Saudi shipping in July.

Only a confirmed 373,000 barrels a day of Saudi crude have transited Bab al-Mandeb so far this month, the lowest level since February, Xu said, with most Yanbu cargoes now heading north via Egypt instead.

If Hormuz were shut and the Houthis blocked all Saudi tankers, Gulf producers could export only through a few pipelines and Yanbu’s northbound route, Xu said.

That would leave about 7.5 million barrels a day of Middle Eastern crude, against 16.8 million now, a shortfall of about 9.3 million barrels a day, she estimated.

“If such attacks occur, the supply disruption could be even more severe and prolonged,” Xu said, referring to strikes on oilfields, terminals and pipelines.

Not for long – possibly just weeks, according to experts.

If Kpler’s estimated shortfall had to be covered entirely from the roughly 400 million usable barrels that Kildow identified, they could not, in practice, be released that fast. Japanese and South Korean reserves can move quickly, Kildow said, but US barrels are staged over three months, and Europe’s contribution is uncertain.

Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG Group, said the world was fortunate after the first closure. “The salient feature of March and beyond was how a crisis didn’t actually develop. We got away with it,” he said.

“I don’t think the global economy will be as lucky next time if there is a protracted conflict,” Beauchamp said. “A month or two is all we have.”

The world would not literally run out of oil. Instead, prices would rise until enough demand disappeared. “One hundred fifty dollars [per barrel] becomes a very distinct possibility, which then sees significant demand destruction,” Beauchamp said.

The sharpest squeeze would be on diesel, which is already nearly double the price of crude, the IEA said.

Refiners would compete for crude grades rich in diesel, “a cost that ultimately lands on consumers,” Kildow said.

Most Gulf exports in September and October went to Asian buyers, and India and Pakistan are among the most exposed, Kildow said, adding that their nearest alternative supply, from West Africa, is 25 to 28 days away by sea, compared with two days from Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates.

“The squeeze won’t hit uniformly. It lands fastest and hardest where reserves are thinnest and substitute supply is farthest away,” Kildow said.

In the second quarter of this year, as the US-Iran war was under way, ExxonMobil reported earnings of $14.5bn, its highest in four years while Chevron posted $12bn, its best in six years and Shell more than doubled its earnings to nearly $10bn. Their profits are largely down to the high oil prices.

A second shock would send refiners scrambling for supplies from the US, Latin America, West Africa and Russia, Xu said.

“This would allow non-Middle Eastern producers to benefit from higher crude prices, potentially alongside lower transportation costs,” she said.

In August, US President Donald Trump said companies such as ExxonMobil and Chevron were “making too much money based on a shortage”.

articles.title: Tiny Caribbean island of Nevis to restore Alexander Hamilton museum with U.S. funds
articles.summary: The Caribbean island of Nevis has received a financial boost in honor of one of its most famous sons, Alexander Hamilton, who went on to become a founding father of the United States and America’s first treasury secretary.
articles.body: HAVANA — The Caribbean island of Nevis has received a financial boost in honor of one of its most famous sons, Alexander Hamilton, who went on to become a founding father of the United States and America’s first treasury secretary. The U.S. government this month awarded $245,000 to restore the home where some believe Hamilton once lived as the U.S. celebrates its 250th anniversary. Hamilton was born on Nevis in the mid-18th century and spent his childhood living at his adopted father’s home in Charlestown. The 17th-century Georgian stone building is now Hamilton House, a museum that houses documents from the famous forefather’s early years and features exhibits honoring other Caribbean personalities. But it has demanded constant repairs: time and salty air have damaged the woodwork. Nevis Premier Mark Brantley told The Associated Press on Wednesday that he’s grateful for the funds. “We have tried valiantly as locals to preserve these very important historical monuments,” he said. Despite Hamilton having lived only the early part of his childhood in Nevis, the premier believes his legacy is inspiring. “Hamilton is significant because I think it’s a demonstration of what a small island like Nevis, a little dot in the ocean, can contribute to the founding of the greatest nation in the world, the United States,” Brantley said. The two-story, Georgian stone building that was originally built around 1680 was destroyed by an earthquake in 1840 and was last restored in 1983. Brantley said the restoration work is important to both the U.S. and Nevis: “Hamilton remains, I think, an iconic figure for us and a figure that we can look at his legacy and inspire our own people to achieve and to know that greatness is available for all of us.”

articles.title: The Indian workers filming their work to train AI
articles.summary: Indian workers are being paid to film themselves at work and the footage is used to train AI.
articles.body:
Mohammed Ashim has been cutting hair and trimming beards for four years in Bengaluru.

But recently the 22-year old has been strapping a camera to his head to record his work.

The camera only records his hands and fingers - his client's faces are blurred out.

"The routine is simple, but you have to be disciplined about how you move. The operations team taught me that my hands always have to stay cleanly inside the frame, the lighting has to be sharp, and I can't tilt my head too abruptly while working."

He wears the camera for five or six hours a day.

"It's good money, but honestly, the feeling of doing something this futuristic is what keeps me excited. I never imagined my razor techniques would be useful to a global tech company," says Ashim.

He is one of hundreds of thousands of workers across the world paid to record their activities.

Ashim's footage is collected by a local company, which might have hundreds of people filming their work.

That video is then sold on to technology companies and research organisations who use it to train artificial intelligence - in particular so-called physical AI, a type of artificial intelligence that can control robots in the real world.

Rashdan Technologies collects and processes such human generated data.

"Every robotics company, every frontier AI lab, has a specific kind of data they want: industrial tasks, agriculture, household chores, small business work like pottery, garment-making, embroidery, candle-making. We go wherever the task is," says co-founder and CEO Shahil Baig.

His company pays $5 to $10 (£3.74; £7.47) for eight to 10 hours of recorded work.

"For a lot of these people, that's meaningful," Baig says.

Making sure workers give their consent and are comfortable with the process is important, he says.

"We record hands, not faces, and where multi-camera rigs do capture more of the body or environment, we blur faces out. No names, no contact details, nothing that identifies them personally goes into what we hand off."

But his customers are getting more demanding.

"Now clients are asking for four to six cameras rigged around a person's head to cover the entire scene, not just the hands.

"Getting someone to agree to one small camera is one conversation. Getting them to agree to wearing what's effectively a five-camera headset is a completely different, and harder, one. We pay more for that tier of data collection because of what we're asking of people."

And the industry is becoming more crowded, Agarwal expects dozens more competitors to emerge in India this year.

If you want robots to navigate the real world, they can't just be trained inside computer simulations, argues Manish Agarwal, the founder of Humyn Labs, which collects and processes human-generated data.

Most of that data comes from video, but sometimes collectors wear hardware on their hands and fingers to capture physical contact.

"Physical tasks require high-quality signals involving limb movements, fingers, wrists, elbows, shoulders and dynamic force application. For example: applying the correct grip force so a plastic bottle doesn't crumble versus a steel glass," he says.

And until recently, that data was not available.

"There is no existing internet archive of embodied human activity - no dataset of a kitchen being cleaned, or a car being assembled by hands that know exactly how much force to apply. That data has to be captured from scratch, in the real world, across diverse environments," says Agarwal, whose company has bases in Bangalore and San Francisco.

At the moment his firm has 96,000 data collectors across countries in Latin America and Southeast Asia.

Humyn Labs filters the thousands of hours of video supplied by those collectors, selecting the most useful content. It's then labelled so the AI knows what it is looking at and packaged in a format that can be used by clients.

"You need to source across a variety of factories, a variety of tasks, in different geographies because if you want to build deployment for US factories or US houses, you'd want environments that are a proxy for that. Residential houses in India may not be the right context for building a robotics use case for the US."

But are workers collecting data for machines that will one day do their jobs?

At the moment it's too early to tell says Bino Paul, senior professor at the School of Management and Labour Studies at the Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS) in Mumbai.

For some workers AI might be a useful tool, but robots could automate other jobs, he says.

The problem is that, if machines do start to take over, there will be little workers can do about.

"By the time workers realise what they have participated in, things may have gone too far," he says.

Like many others, he wants governments to regulate AI.

"AI cannot be viewed merely as a technical system. We need to develop a socio-technical system in which ethics is upheld through human agency, ensuring that AI delivers beneficence rather than maleficence."

Despite concerns over where AI is heading, money is still being poured into its development.

Some of that trickles down to workers in India, where there is no shortage of workers prepared to wear a camera for a few dollars a day.

Mohammed Arman has been working in the textiles industry in Bangalore for 10 years.

"Garments stitching and cutting. I know this work so well I could probably do it with my eyes closed. Cloth, thread, needle, machine after 10 years, your hands just know what to do before your mind even tells them," he says.

He has recently started wearing a head-mounted camera that records his work.

"For me, it's simple. This is survival. I have a family back home in Bihar, and every rupee I send back matters. If someone offers me extra money to wear a camera while I do the exact same work I've been doing for 10 years, I'm not going to say no.

"It doesn't cost me anything. I'm already doing the stitching, already doing the cutting. Now I just get paid a little more for it," he says.

While there is demand for such footage it will be collected somewhere.

"India's current role in this industry is largely as a supplier of raw material - people strap on cameras, record themselves doing ordinary tasks, and that footage gets shipped off to labs abroad," Agarwal says.

But he argues the value of that kind of work will quickly become eroded, as more companies compete for collection contracts.

"India can't afford to stay a footage supplier. It needs to move up the value chain: from recording raw video to owning the pipeline that turns that video into something usable - cleaning it, structuring it, validating it, and ultimately setting the standards for what counts as high-quality training data," he says.

For some people collecting data is attractive part time work.

Science teacher Jolly Arifur was looking for work she could do from home that would fit around her young son.

"For the past seven months, I strapped a rig-mounted camera on my head while doing my routine domestic work scrubbing, cooking, sweeping tile floors, and folding laundry."

Arifur, who lives in Guntakal, Anantapur, fits the recording work around her teaching.

"I get paid two to three dollars per hour. If I record three to five hours a day, that's a good amount in hand it's become an extra source of income for me, on top of teaching. I'm managing both honestly, fantastically."

articles.title: Two suspected gunmen dead, two IDF soldiers killed in West Bank shooting
articles.summary: Two suspected gunmen were killed by the IDF after a shooting near Judea Junction in the southern West Bank left five Israelis wounded on Friday.
articles.body: Two Israeli Defense Forces soldiers were killed and three other people were wounded by two suspected gunmen, who were also killed, in a shooting Friday in the southern West Bank, officials said. Staff Sergeant Ron Yonatan Roytman, aged 23, from Ashkelon, a squad commander in the Ari Battalion (775), Search and Rescue Brigade and Sergeant Yuval Shai Svilem, aged 20, from Hod Hasharon, a combat soldier in the Ari Battalion, Search and Rescue Brigade, both died as a result of the attack, according to the Israel Defense Forces. The IDF reported that it responded to a shooting in the Judea Junction area Friday and killed two people it identified as "terrorists." Hours after the attack, Israel ordered the army to prepare for a full closure of the West Bank, according to the Associated Press. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held an emergency meeting of his Security Cabinet, claiming Hamas was "planning a major attack aimed at murdering innocent civilians." Netanyahu also said a large scale operation in the West Bank is to begin soon. Israeli intelligence groups and security forces conducted dozens of raids throughout the West Bank on Friday, apprehending dozens of people, including those who Israeli officials claimed were members of Hamas and affiliated with Islamic Jihad. articles.title: Snapchat billionaire Evan Spiegel and wife Miranda Kerr help erase $550 million in medical debt for 261,000 Californians struggling to pay bills, now turning to LA wildfire survivors
articles.summary: Snapchat co-founder and Snap Inc.
articles.body: Snapchat co-founder and Snap Inc. CEO Evan Spiegel and his wife, Australian model and entrepreneur Miranda Kerr, have helped erase $550 million in medical debt owed by more than 261,000 Californians. The couple made a multimillion-dollar donation to Undue Medical Debt, a nonprofit that purchases qualifying medical debt for a fraction of its original value before cancelling it. Their philanthropic efforts also extend to Los Angeles, where devastating wildfires in January 2025 destroyed thousands of structures, including Spiegel’s childhood home in Pacific Palisades. More than a year after the disaster, the couple continues to support recovery initiatives for affected residents and research into the fires’ long-term health consequences. Spiegel was honoured for his philanthropic work at an awards ceremony in Washington, DC, on October 13, 2026.Snapchat billionaire helps erase $550 million in medical debtSpiegel and Kerr’s medical debt relief initiative was announced in June 2026 and reported by the Los Angeles Times. Their contribution helped Undue Medical Debt cancel more than $550 million in outstanding medical bills for over 261,000 Californians.The nonprofit acquires medical debt in bulk from hospitals, physician groups, collection agencies and other creditors, often paying substantially less than the original amount owed. It then cancels the acquired debt, allowing eligible individuals to receive relief without having to repay the outstanding balance.According to the organisation, people generally qualify if their household income is at or below 400% of the federal poverty level or if their medical debt represents at least 5% of their annual income. Recipients do not need to apply individually because the nonprofit identifies and purchases qualifying debts in bulk.The $550 million figure represents the face value of the debt cancelled, rather than the amount donated by the couple. Their precise contribution has not been publicly disclosed.The initiative reached communities across California. San Diego County received approximately $99 million in medical debt relief, benefiting 40,369 people, while Los Angeles County saw $26.7 million in debt cancelled for 17,466 residents, according to figures reported by the Los Angeles Times.Spiegel turns to Los Angeles wildfire recoveryThe couple’s philanthropy has also focused on communities devastated by the January 2025 wildfires in Los Angeles County. Spiegel grew up in Pacific Palisades, where his childhood home was destroyed during the disaster.The fires killed dozens of people and destroyed more than 16,000 structures, according to early assessments. The destruction left thousands of residents facing the lengthy process of securing assistance, assessing damage and rebuilding their homes.The disaster also affected Spiegel’s company. In an interview with PEOPLE published on October 15, 2026, he said more than 100 Snap employees had been affected by the fires.In January 2025, Spiegel, Snap and Snapchat co-founder Bobby Murphy contributed $5 million in immediate aid. The support formed part of a wider philanthropic response to the disaster.Recalling the moment he learnt that his childhood home was burning, Spiegel told PEOPLE that his sister alerted the family after seeing the house on television. He described the experience as surreal, particularly because the house was where he and Murphy had started Snapchat.Department of Angels supports wildfire survivorsSpiegel also helped launch the Department of Angels, a nonprofit established to support Los Angeles wildfire recovery. The California Community Foundation, Snap, Spiegel and Murphy committed a combined $10 million in seed funding to establish the initiative, the Los Angeles Times reported.The organisation works to connect affected residents with resources, support community-led recovery and bring survivors’ concerns to decision-makers at the local, state and federal levels.Its work comes as many residents continue to face obstacles in rebuilding their homes and returning to their neighbourhoods. In August 2026, The Guardian reported that thousands of wildfire survivors were still waiting for more than $15 billion in federal recovery assistance.Spiegel told PEOPLE that the delays remained frustrating and stressed that the recognition of his philanthropic work should not overshadow the needs of affected communities.Couple fund research into long-term health effects of the firesBeyond immediate financial assistance, the Spiegel Family Fund supported the launch of the Los Angeles Fire Human Exposure and Long-Term Health Study, also known as the L.A. Fire HEALTH Study, in January 2025.The 10-year research initiative brings together scientists from institutions including UCLA, Harvard University, the University of California, Davis, and the University of Texas at Austin. Researchers are investigating pollutants released during the fires, how they spread through air, soil, dust and water, and the possible short- and long-term health consequences of exposure.The study also aims to provide evidence that can help residents understand the risks of returning to affected homes and neighbourhoods. Urban fires can burn synthetic materials, household products and building components, potentially releasing a complex mixture of pollutants.The findings could help communities better prepare for future urban wildfires and guide decisions about environmental monitoring and recovery. Researchers will need to follow exposed populations over time to establish the nature and extent of any lasting health effects.Spiegel and Kerr involve their children in charitable workThe couple have also sought to make community service part of family life. Spiegel and Kerr are raising three sons together, Hart, Myles and Pierre. Kerr also has a son, Flynn, from her previous marriage to actor Orlando Bloom.Speaking to PEOPLE, Spiegel said the family tries to involve their children in activities such as packing meals and baking cookies for a local women's shelter.He said he wants his children to understand that their opportunities come with a responsibility to help people who are less fortunate. Kerr, he added, has inspired him through her care for others since the early days of their relationship.Their philanthropic interests extend beyond medical debt and disaster recovery. In 2022, the couple helped pay off student loans for the graduating class at Otis College of Art and Design in Los Angeles. Spiegel's wider giving also includes support for creative education and opportunities for young people through the Spiegel Family Fund and the Snap Foundation.Evan Spiegel honoured for philanthropy in WashingtonOn October 13, 2026, Spiegel was honoured at the eighth annual George H.W. Bush Points of Light Awards in Washington, DC. The ceremony recognised individuals for their philanthropic work, volunteering and contributions to communities across the United States.Other honourees included David M. Rubenstein, co-founder of investment firm The Carlyle Group, and Olivia Zhang, founder and CEO of Cancer Kids First.Reflecting on the recognition, Spiegel told PEOPLE that he was grateful for what had been accomplished but believed it was important to acknowledge how much more work remained. He specifically pointed to wildfire survivors still waiting for federal assistance.He also spoke about the importance of helping others, describing people as interconnected and saying that this creates an obligation to support one another. articles.title: Netanyahu orders closure of West Bank after two soldiers killed in shooting attack
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the closure of the occupied West Bank after two Palestinian gunmen opened fire Friday on an Israeli military checkpoint, killing two soldiers.
articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the closure of the occupied West Bank after two Palestinian gunmen opened fire Friday on an Israeli military checkpoint, killing two soldiers. Three more soldiers were lightly wounded in the attack, according to the Israel Defense Forces (IDF). The attack came just four days before Israel holds elections for the first time since the Hamas-led attack on October 7, 2023, in a crucial test for Netanyahu, who has sought to portray himself as a security hardliner. The IDF said it was imposing “a full siege” on the city of Hebron after the attack and Netanyahu said he had ordered a full closure of the West Bank starting Friday. But it was unclear exactly when such a full closure would begin or how long it would last. There are over 900 Israeli military checkpoints, gates and barriers across the West Bank. And while closures and restrictions around checkpoints between Palestinian cities and villages are routine in the territory, especially around Jewish holidays and significant events, Israel lacks the forces to shut down every checkpoint and impose a complete closure that would fully prevent the movement of Palestinians. A full closure will also prevent Palestinians with Israeli identification cards or work permits from entering Israel, but that number is already extremely limited. Both gunmen were shot and killed, the IDF said in a statement, as forces continued searches across the area for anyone else who may be connected to the attack. Videos from the scene depict a firefight between the Palestinian gunmen and Israeli forces that lasted at least several minutes with repeated bursts of gunfire ringing out. In one Reuters video, an Israeli responder yells that the shooting has been going on for at least 20 minutes and they were struggling to remove the wounded from the scene. The IDF said it located a vehicle used by the gunmen to carry out the attack, which was filled with “a large quantity” of ammunition. “This was a serious terror attack,” said IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir following a situation assessment. “The fighters’ rapid action prevented an even more serious attack and further harm to civilians and security forces.” He said the ammunition in the car was intended to be used “to carry out an attack on a much larger scale.” Zamir said the IDF would also carry out further arrests of suspects and increase intelligence operations in the area. “We will pursue Hamas terrorists and those who sent them, wherever they are and at all times,” Netanyahu said in a statement. Netanyahu later on Friday said the military would forcefully evacuate the area and “transform it completely,” adding that Israel would employ the plan used in the Jenin, Tulkarm, Nur Shams, and Al-Far’a refugee camps in early 2025, which led to the displacement of thousands of Palestinians and the evacuation of entire neighborhoods. “That is exactly what we will do here, in a neighborhood in Hebron from which the terrorists came. We will evacuate the residents, go house to house, remove weapons found there, and address and destroy all terrorist infrastructure,” he said. Hamas praised the attack in a statement but did not claim responsibility. “Together with all the people of Israel, I pray for the full and speedy recovery of those wounded in the attack,” said Netanyahu’s main rival, former IDF Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, said in a statement on X. CNN’s Dana Karni and Kara Fox contributed reporting.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV cancels Assisi trip on doctors’ advice as he recovers from surgery
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV will miss a planned trip to Assisi next week on doctors’ orders as he continues recovering from thoracic surgery, the Vatican said.
articles.body: VATICAN CITY — Pope Leo XIV will miss a planned trip to Assisi next week on doctors’ orders as he continues recovering from thoracic surgery he underwent last Tuesday, the Vatican said Friday. The pope had been due to attend an Oct. 27 gathering marking the 40th anniversary of St. John Paul II’s World Day of Prayer for Peace. In a statement, the Vatican said Leo was advised not to travel “to facilitate his recovery” from the surgery. The pope will instead send a message to organizers, Christian and other religious leaders, and guests attending the event, titled “Disarmed and Disarming Peace.” The Vatican said Leo wanted to express his closeness to participants and reaffirm his belief that the “spirit of Assisi,” dialogue and the search for words and gestures of peace remain valuable resources at a time of conflict. The Assisi meeting commemorates the landmark interfaith peace gathering convened by St. John Paul II in 1986. The cancellation is the latest change to Leo’s schedule since he underwent thoracic surgery last week. The Vatican has said the pope’s activities will be guided by medical advice during his recovery. Pope Leo will need no further treatment for lung cancer after tests confirmed the disease was localized, the Vatican said Wednesday. Leo, 71, had part of one lung removed last week in the first major health event of his 17-month pontificate. The surgery confirmed he had adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer. Leo returned to the Vatican last Saturday, as his surgeon said there are “no clinical reasons” to prevent a planned trip to Latin America next month. Thoracic surgeons often advise patients not to fly for three weeks after surgery — which would give the pope just the interval needed to make his planned Nov. 6-17 trip to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, depending on his recovery. The trip will involve a dozen flights and two helicopter rides to high altitudes. In his public appearances since returning to the Vatican, Leo appeared in good health, speaking with a strong and clear voice.

articles.title: Ukrainian officials say Starshield restrictions still in place, despite Trump’s claims
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Thursday claimed that Elon Musk had restored Ukraine’s access to a military-grade version of his Starlink internet service, called Starshield, but Ukrainian officials have said restrictions remain in place that are complicating Kyiv’s war effort.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Thursday claimed that Elon Musk had restored Ukraine’s access to a military-grade version of his Starlink internet service, called Starshield, but Ukrainian officials have said restrictions remain in place that are complicating Kyiv’s war effort. Trump asked Musk in a phone call in recent days to restore Ukraine’s full access to the Starshield satellite system, a person familiar with the matter told CNN. Trump had been seeking out information about the slowdown and went to Musk after Ukrainian officials reported disruptions, the source said. However, Trump has declined to comment on the call publicly, telling reporters at the White House, “Whether I called or whether somebody else called, doesn’t make any difference, I guess. The bottom line – he put it back.” But those restrictions remain in place despite the comments from Trump, Ukrainian officials said on Friday morning. For more than a week, the restrictions have disrupted any military ordnance moving at high speeds – hindering interceptor drones in defending against Russian attacks and upending Ukrainian military operations in many areas of the front line, Ukrainian officials have said. “At this time, we are not observing any lifting of restrictions on Starlink,” said Serhiy Beskrestnov, an adviser to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. “There are isolated cases where Starlink may operate slightly faster than the restrictions allow, but this is likely due to the SpaceX algorithm or specific usage conditions, rather than a lifting of the restrictions.” A Ukrainian Defense Ministry source told CNN on Friday morning that “there is currently no confirmation that the restrictions have been lifted” and “instances of signal loss are still being observed” for any military ordnance travelling above 100 miles per hour (161 kilometers per hour). “There are definitely speed limits; nothing has changed yet, at least from what I can see here,” a Ukrainian Armed Forces officer told CNN. “It makes coordination difficult; sometimes there are interruptions. The connection drops out for 10 to 15 seconds.” “We lost a lot of assets, much more than usual,” the officer added, saying the restrictions have affected reconnaissance drones and drones with Starlink-equipped systems on board. A third source familiar with the situation told CNN on Thursday afternoon that speeds are not unlimited, and any restored access is “clearly not enough to intercept jet-powered drones” launched by Russia. Ukraine is waiting for information and clarification from the US side about the situation and there is no response yet, the source said. Trump and some of his top officials had denied making the call to throttle Ukraine’s use of the Starshield service, without offering any clear explanation for what had actually happened. Earlier this week, Trump said he was not involved. Musk also denied taking unilateral action, pointing the finger toward the Trump administration. “Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” he said in a social media post last week. The Wall Street Journal first reported that Trump called Musk last week to request he restore Ukraine’s full access to the satellite communications network. Trump on Thursday declined to answer questions about the phone call, even as he claimed Musk had restored access. “I don’t want to comment one way or the other, but my relationship with Elon is a very good one,” the US president said. Russian attacks persist while Ukrainian interceptors hindered While Ukrainian defenses remain hampered by the Starshield restrictions, Russian attacks using jet-powered drones and other strike drones have continued. Russia launched 176 attack drones on Thursday night and in the overnight hours, according to the Ukrainian Air Force. At least nine civilians have been killed and 76 injured in the last day, according to a CNN tally of local officials’ reports across the country. The deputy energy minister of Ukraine said that Russian attacks targeted energy infrastructure in six regions, leaving more than 500,000 people without power on Friday. The country’s State Emergency Service also said a series of attacks on the Sumy region hit civilian infrastructure and residential areas. Russia’s Ministry of Defense said it hit a railcar depot used by the Ukrainian Armed Forces in the central Poltava region and the Danube River port of Vylkove in southern Ukraine. Russia also intercepted and destroyed 443 Ukrainian drones overnight, the Russian defense ministry said. Three civilians were injured by falling debris in Russia’s Nizhny Novgorod region, according to the local governor on Friday. This story has been updated with additional developments.

articles.title: Israel orders ‘full lockdown’ of occupied West Bank after 2 soldiers killed in shooting attack
articles.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered a “full lockdown” of the occupied West Bank on Friday after Israel’s military said it killed two Palestinians accused of launching a shooting attack that killed two soldiers and injured three others in the city of Hebron.
articles.body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered a “full lockdown” of the occupied West Bank on Friday after Israel’s military said it killed two Palestinians accused of launching a shooting attack that killed two soldiers and injured three others in the city of Hebron. The deadly incident comes just days before a crucial election that will decide whether Netanyahu can hold on to power. There has been a recent surge in Israeli settler violence and military activity in the West Bank centered on the start of the olive harvesting season, with Palestinians, activists and American journalists among those attacked and detained. Netanyahu’s office said it instructed the Israel Defense Forces to “impose a closure” on Hebron and to prepare for a “full lockdown” across the entire West Bank starting Friday. It gave no further details on the planned closure of the territory. In comments following an emergency meeting with his security cabinet and top military and security officials, Netanyahu blamed Hamas for the shooting and said the militant group was “planning a major attack aimed at murdering innocent civilians.” He cited “large quantities of weapons and ammunition discovered,” but did not provide further details on the attack. He did not say whether the injured included soldiers or civilians. The order to lock down the West Bank came hours after the Israeli military said it had killed two people after a shooting attack in which at least five people were initially reported injured. The Israeli military later said two soldiers had been killed in the attack. It said three additional soldiers were lightly injured and evacuated to receive medical treatment at a hospital. The military said the gunmen had been armed with an M16 rifle and a handgun and that “numerous” soldiers would be operating in the area following the incident. Magen David Adom, Israel’s primary emergency service, had earlier said it received a report at around 7:15 a.m. local time (12:15 a.m. ET) of multiple casualties following the attack near the Yehuda Junction, near Hebron. It said first responders had provided medical treatment to at least five people, including two in critical condition. The identities of the two people alleged to have launched the attack and who were killed by Israeli forces were not immediately clear as of late Friday morning. The lockdown comes ahead of next week’s Israeli election, which is largely viewed as a referendum on Netanyahu’s leadership around the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attacks. Netanyahu has focused much of campaign in the lead-up to Tuesday’s vote on security for Israelis. His government has repeatedly warned of potential attacks by the country’s “enemies” in the lead-up to the election, without providing evidence. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz suggested there would be a sweeping offensive in Hebron, comparing it to Israel’s deadly assault in Gaza and its operations Lebanon, as well as in the Jenin refugee camp in the northern West Bank. “Every clan neighborhood in Hebron from which the terrorists emerged today will be evacuated of its residents, and the terror infrastructure in the neighborhood will be addressed and dismantled,” he said. “This is the only language that jihadist terrorism understands. Just like in Gaza, just like in Lebanon.” Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel’s far-right national security minister, called Friday for the Palestinian Authority, the governing body that has long overseen parts of the occupied West Bank, to be dismantled in response to the attack. “There cannot be a situation where, within Judea and Samaria, we have a state of terror,” he said in a post on X, using a name employed by some Israelis for the area. Far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich shared similar sentiments, saying there was “no avoiding a comprehensive military campaign” in the West Bank to “dismantle the Palestinian authority, collect weapons, and eliminate terrorists — just as in Gaza and Lebanon.” The West Bank has been a growing flashpoint for months, and the past week has seen another wave of settler violence and military activity in the territory as the Palestinian olive harvesting season has gotten underway. American nationals are among those who have come under attack while accompanying Palestinian farmers on their harvests. Earlier this week, New York congressional candidate Brad Lander was detained in the area alongside a number of activists and American rabbis. Settler violence has long flared during the olive harvesting season, but in the years since the Oct. 7 attacks, violence has increased sharply, with Palestinians also seeing their olives stolen. According to the United Nations, at least 160 Israeli settler attacks linked to the olive harvesting season were recorded in the first two weeks of October alone. The U.N. said many of those attacks were carried out “under the protection of, or with the participation of, Israeli forces.” Netanyahu’s government has backed settler expansion in the West Bank despite international condemnation. The mounting settler violence has increasingly been described as terrorism by some global officials, including by U.S. ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee.
